A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRAME benchmark and study of visual biases in LVLM judges. Their full text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of eight LVLM judges, prompting mitigation, pairwise comparisons, and combined visual biases, including additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds o3 evaluations, bias-definition prompting, triple-bias results, and inter-annotator correlation measurements.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a bias-definition prompting variant that supplies the manipulation name and definition to the judge, extending the generic bias-aware prompt (Figure 6). This changes the mitigation procedure's inputs; FRAME construction and the eight underlying visual manipulations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same 500-instance FRAME benchmark, five domains, and scoring and pairwise tasks are retained. Table 6 extends the tested input conditions to images carrying three simultaneous visual biases, beyond v1's single- and dual-bias conditions.

E2.justification: o3 joins the existing eight judges, with evaluated results in Tables 3–4 and Figure 2. Table 5 adds bias-definition prompting alongside the retained standard, bias-aware, and CoT comparison conditions.

E3.justification: Section 6 extends the reported combination search from all bias pairs to pairs and triples and adds an explicit bias-definition prompting condition. Existing sample counts, scoring metrics, and order-reversed pairwise evaluation remain unchanged. The newly described pilot and greedy search document parameter selection without establishing a revision to existing experiments.

E4.justification: The mitigation analysis now tests whether explicitly identifying and defining the bias reduces susceptibility, while the combination analysis tests the effect of adding a third manipulation. Appendix A also adds annotation-reliability analysis. These extend existing analyses without replacing them.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly reports Pearson and Spearman correlations between two human annotators, with coefficients ranging from 0.585 to 0.816 in Table 7. This adds statistical reliability reporting; neither version provides confidence intervals or repeated-run uncertainty estimates for the judge experiments.

E6.justification: Previously tabulated scores are retained, including the Combined bias column renamed Dual bias. Added results include o3, bias-definition prompting, triple biases, and annotator correlations. For example, the new bias-definition condition reports 1.4% instruction-overlay inflation in Table 5. Triple-bias scores exceed dual-bias scores only in People and Indoor, declining in the other three domains.

T1.justification: The conceptual bias definitions and attack-success definition are retained. Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations, and the new correlation reporting introduces no theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: FRAME, eight visual biases, widespread judge susceptibility, vulnerability in pairwise evaluation, and incomplete mitigation through prompting. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v1 speculates that stacking three or more biases could further increase distortion. v2 replaces this with domain-dependent amplification or saturation and proposes a perceptual-noise threshold as a possible explanation. Appendix A also adds a rationale for why co-author annotation should have limited influence on bias findings; the Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: The code/data footnote replaces TBD with a specific repository address. Appendices A–B disclose two English-fluent co-author annotators, pilot-based parameter narrowing and greedy selection, the o3 model snapshot, and the new prompt template. These are useful documentation additions, although detailed o3 and triple-bias recipes are absent.

R1.justification: v2 adds the OpenAI o3/o4-mini reference and removes Yarom et al. (2023) from the compositional-evaluation discussion and bibliography. The broader related-work organization and first-systematic-study positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized rewriting of the mitigation and combined-bias discussion, expanded appendix explanations, an acknowledgement section, and small wording corrections. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3–6 and Figure 2 expand to display the added conditions and judge. v2 adds the annotation-reliability table and bias-definition prompt figure, relocates existing appendix prompt displays, and updates numbering. The established visual design and most figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The new mitigation and triple-bias experiments strengthen the analysis, particularly by replacing speculation about further stacking with evidence of domain-dependent effects. Annotation-agreement statistics, clearer implementation disclosures, and a concrete code/data pointer improve transparency. These are limited gains within an otherwise stable study; missing detailed recipes for o3 and triple-bias experiments constrain reproducibility of the additions.
